{{Quote|For every stormtrooper you kill here today, a Rebel life is saved tomorrow.|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]]|<ref name="NEGWT">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>}}
The '''DF.9''' was an [[Anti-Infantry Turret|anti-infantry battery]] produced by [[Golan Arms/Legends|Golan Arms]]. Used extensively throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] by both the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], the DF.9 was used to protect vital military installations. The Alliance installed several DF.9s as part of their defensive emplacements protecting [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. During the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the arrayed DF.9s were not enough to stop the advance of the Empire's [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transports]].

==Description==
Manufactured by [[Golan Arms/Legends|Golan Arms]], the DF.9 was a fixed emplacement anti-[[Infantry/Legends|infantry]] weapon. It incorporated a single [[DF.9 laser cannon]] mounted atop a four-[[Meter/Legends|meter]] tall cylindrical housing. The rotating turret housed the weapon's armored [[Blaster gas/Legends|blaster gas]] [[Gas chamber|chamber]], which fed into the [[Laser Excitation Chamber]], through the [[Laser actuator/Legends|laser actuator]] and into the first-stage [[Barrel/Legends|barrel]] before being released through the laser barrel. A [[Cooling unit/Legends|cooling unit]] and [[Intake|cooling vents]] were also located in the turret.<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

[[File:DF9_Schematics.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Schematics for the DF.9]]
The tower was composed of heavily-[[Armor/Legends|armored]] [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]],<ref name="FF83" /> with [[proton-shield]]ing<ref name="EGWT" /> that was resistant to close-quarters [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire<ref name="RASB" /> but useless against the firepower of an [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]].<ref name="FF89">{{FactFile|89|ANT 3-4|Golan Arms DF.9 Anti Infantry Battery}}</ref> The tower featured a front panel for access,<ref name="FF83" /> an upper observation hatch,<ref name="RECG" /> and room for the [[proton shield generator]],<ref name="NEGWT" /> [[Targeting computer/Legends|targeting computers]], and [[Power core/Legends|power core]]. Shield projectors for the [[proton-shield]]ing were installed on both the turret and tower.<ref name="EGWT" />

The turreted laser cannon employed precision targeting computers, and had a one-hundred and eighty degree rotation. The optimal range for the DF.9 was three [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], although the laser cannon was capable of hitting targets at a distance of sixteen kilometers<ref name="EGWT" /> at the cost of decreased accuracy.<ref name="NEGWT" /> The DF.9 was capable of firing a shot every three [[Standard second|seconds]],<ref name="EGWT" /> although the beam diverged and degraded over its maximum range.<ref name="FF83" /> The impact of the energy beam scattered explosive energy<ref name="EGWT" /> and produced a secondary blast of [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]]. The collateral effect<ref name="FF83" /> produced an eight-meter radius impact point that could effectively destroy entire [[Squad/Legends|squads]] of [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]]. The weapon produced more destructive firepower than [[Heavy repeating blaster/Legends|heavy repeating blasters]] such as the [[E-Web heavy repeating blaster/Legends|E-Web heavy repeating blaster]].<ref name="EGWT" />

[[File:EchoBaseDefenses.jpg|thumb|right|280px|A DF.9 overlooking the trenches on Hoth.]]
The DF.9 required a crew of three to operate; a [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]]<ref name="EGWT" /> who sat in the upper turret,<ref name="GG3">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref> a targeting computer [[Technician/Legends|technician]], and a technician to monitor the energy flow from the [[Power generator/Legends|power generator]],<ref name="EGWT" /> who were both stationed in the armored tower.<ref name="GG3" /> The turret could be crewed by a single gunner, but the efficiency of the weapon was diminished.<ref name="NEGWT" /> Skilled gunners could use the DF.9's accuracy to effectively disable [[Army/Legends|army]] support systems and light vehicles,<ref name="NEGWT" /> and it was devastating to foot soldiers and a threat to vehicles such as the [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transport]].<ref name="GG3" />

The DF.9 was best used in conjunction with other similar units and anti-vehicle lasers to defend military bases, [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] and other strategic installations.<ref name="EGWT" /> It could be installed on multiple terrain types,<ref name="EaWPrima">[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Empire at War'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> but the nature of the DF.9's fixed emplacement meant that the unit was not able to be moved easily.<ref name="EGWT" />

The DF.9 spawned several variants, including the [[SP.9 Anti-Infantry Artillery Vehicle]], the [[Twin DF.9/Legends|Twin DF.9]],<ref name="ISB">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> the [[Twin SP.9]],<ref name="RASB" /> and the [[DF.9/B]].<ref name="ISB" />

==History==
[[File:CannonsDestroyed-Republic57.png|thumb|left|330px|The Galactic Republic's DF.9 cannons are destroyed during the Battle of Jabiim.]]
The DF.9 saw some usage during [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. During the [[Battle of Jabiim]], multiple DF.9s were established outside [[Cobalt Station]]. However, the Republic's DF.9s and defenses outside the station proved to be ineffective against the overwhelming forces of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]],<ref name="Republic 57">[[Republic 57|''Republic'' 57]]</ref> helping to pave the way for the battle's end as a major Republic defeat.<ref name="FF 128">{{FactFile|128|JAB 3-4|Battle of Jabiim}}</ref> Many years after the Clone Wars,<ref name="Empire 30">[[Empire 30|''Empire'' 30]]</ref> the DF.9 was a popular unit in service during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and it was found in the militaries of both the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]],<ref name="EGWT" /> where it was the standard [[Anti-Infantry Turret|anti-infantry battery]] in use by the latter.<ref name="RASB" />

The use of the DF.9 by the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] raised Golan Arms' stature with the Empire more than any sales brochures. However, the supply contracts were slowly taken from Golan Arms and given to companies that were run by either friends or relatives of those Imperial [[Officer/Legends|officers]] in charge. Subsequently, Golan Arms approached the Alliance about supplying them with the DF.9. Initially happy with the deal, the Alliance became less than enthused when they realized that the limited fire arc of the weapon meant that several had to be purchased and deployed to defend an installation which was a problem for the cash-short Rebellion.<ref name="FF89" />

The units were deployed to several important Alliance bases, including [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], [[Tierfon Rebel Outpost]], [[Haven Base]] on [[Arbra/Legends|Arbra]], and [[Oracle Base]] on [[Tel III]].<ref name="EGWT" /> They were modified by the Alliance to be more effective and efficient against enemy combat vehicles<ref name="RASB" /> by upgrading the [[Laser actuator/Legends|laser actuator]] and first-stage [[Barrel/Legends|barrel]] to channel more energy through the weapon to deliver a more potent [[Laser/Legends|laser]] bolt that was effective against vehicles such as the AT-ST and the [[Compact Assault Vehicle/Wheeled PX-10]].<ref name="EGWT" />

By the time of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the DF.9 was twenty [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old, and was still in use by the New Republic, Imperial factions, and independent entities such as [[Planetary Security Forces|planetary defense forces]], [[Militia/Legends|militias]], and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]]. The units were easily purchased on the [[Black market/Legends|black market]].<ref name="EGWT" /> During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the DF.9 was forty years old, and was generally only used by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and outlaws.<ref name="NEGWT" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Hoth-anti-infantry-mcquarrie.jpg|thumb|200px|DF.9 concept art by Ralph McQuarrie]]
The [[November]] [[2003]] [[The Empire Strikes Back (TCG)|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] expansion set of the ''[[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]'' features an image of the [[Atgar SpaceDefense Corporation/Legends|Atgar SpaceDefense Corporation's]] [[1.4 FD P-Tower/Legends|1.4 FD P-Tower]] laser cannon on the set's [http://www.wizards.com/swtcg/swtcg_autocard.asp?name=Anti-Infantry_Laser_Battery "Anti-Infantry Laser Battery"] card, which actually describes the DF.9 anti-infantry battery. An image of the DF.9 appears on the [http://wizards.com/swtcg/images/esb/antivehicle_laser_cannon.jpg "Antivehicle Laser Cannon"], which describes the 1.4 FD P-Tower.
